solutions.name: Developer distribution
solutions.title: Blowhorn for developer distribution
solutions.headline: Post where developers actually talk.
solutions.lead: Hacker News, GitHub, Reddit and Slack, plus LinkedIn, X and Bluesky, from one queue. Posted as you, at a human pace.
solutions.description: One queue for the networks technical companies use: Hacker News, GitHub, Reddit and Slack, plus LinkedIn, X and Bluesky, posted as you from your own browser.

art.alt: Major Blowhorn, a teal rooster drill sergeant in a campaign hat, pointing and shouting through his gold bullhorn, Caribbean Green sound waves pouring out of it

pains.b: None of the schedulers we checked support Hacker News. GitHub and Slack stay a pile of tabs.
Votes, blast posts and "sent via" badges cost the trust you came to earn.

pains.t: A Slack app nobody can install
pains.b: Assistants that act as themselves need an app in the workspace. A free workspace at its app limit has no room.

gets.b: Hacker News submit and comment, GitHub follow and react, Slack messages, plus LinkedIn, X, Reddit and Bluesky.
It submits stories and comments, nothing else, with at most 2 link submissions per profile per day.

gets.t: No Blowhorn app in your Slack
gets.b: Blowhorn works through your own Slack sign-in and posts as you. No app to install, no bot user to invite.
Types key by key in your own browser, caps itself, and hands every CAPTCHA and 2FA prompt to you.

solutions.prompt: Submit the launch post to Hacker News, react on the GitHub release issue, tell #general in Slack, then --dry-run the rest.
solutions.major: Front page or bust, soldier. Every channel, one voice: yours.

faq.q: Does it vote on Hacker News?
faq.a: Never. It submits stories and comments, nothing else. Link submissions are capped at 2 per profile per day.

faq.q: Does Blowhorn install a Slack app?
faq.a: No. Blowhorn works on Slack through Slack's API and sends as you, with your Slack session linked through the Blowhorn extension or a Slack token you add.

faq.q: How does it post to each network?
faq.a: LinkedIn, X, Reddit and Hacker News: Blowhorn types in your own browser, signed in as you. Slack, Bluesky and GitHub go through their APIs.

faq.q: What about Instagram, TikTok, Facebook and YouTube?
faq.a: Coming soon.

solutions.name: Employee advocacy
solutions.title: Blowhorn for employee advocacy
solutions.headline: Advocacy for the rest of us.
solutions.lead: Real teammates, posting as themselves, from one coordinated queue. No 100-seat minimum.
solutions.description: Employee advocacy for small teams: real people amplifying one post as themselves, from one coordinated queue, without a 100-seat minimum.

art.alt: Platoon Private, an orange chicken in a charcoal cap with a coral rank stripe, holding one bayonet rifle

pains.b: Advocacy suites sell to big companies: quote pricing and seat minimums, like Haiilo's 100 seats.
Teammates get an email with a post to share. By the time they do, the first hour is gone.
Suites center LinkedIn and X. Your audience is also on Hacker News, Reddit, GitHub and Slack.

gets.t: A sound wave from your team
gets.b: Schedule one post and every profile you add amplifies it at the moment you pick, each posting as itself.
Teammates and supporters add their own profiles to your account today. Team invites: Coming soon.
Coordinated so the same post isn't sent from two computers, however many your team runs.

gets.t: One pause for the whole wave
gets.b: Pause one action, one computer or every computer at once. Resume, and due times carry forward.

solutions.prompt: Schedule the announcement for 9:00, have every profile amplify it in the first hour, then --dry-run the wave.
solutions.major: Fall in, platoon. One post, every voice, first hour.

faq.q: Does Blowhorn post for teammates without them?
faq.a: No. A teammate adds their own profile to your account, and Blowhorn posts as that person, never as a bot.

faq.q: Can I invite my team?
faq.a: Team invites are Coming soon. Today teammates and supporters add their own profiles to your account.

faq.q: Will the same post go out twice?
faq.a: Your computers coordinate through one queue, so the same post isn't sent from two of them.

faq.q: Do teammates need a proxy?
faq.a: No. Each teammate posts from their own computer's internet connection, with their own IP address. There is no proxy to buy or set up.

solutions.name: Distributed teams
solutions.title: Blowhorn for distributed teams
solutions.headline: One queue for your whole team. No proxies.
solutions.lead: Teammates anywhere run Blowhorn on their own computers and work from one shared queue. Every post goes out over the poster's own internet connection, so there is no proxy to buy, run or explain.
solutions.description: Blowhorn for distributed teams: one shared queue across your teammates' computers, each posting from its own internet connection and IP address. No proxy to buy or run.

art.alt: A recruit chick in a teal helmet and field pack, sitting cross-legged and typing on a laptop with a Major Blowhorn sticker

pains.b: Tools that post from their own servers, or juggle many profiles in one browser, need an IP address for each account. You pay for every one.
Proxies expire, slow down and get blocked. Someone has to rent them, assign them and notice when one breaks.
Sites can spot a proxy or data center address, and a shared one can carry a stranger's history into your account.

gets.b: Each post leaves from the computer that runs it, over that teammate's own internet connection. Your account keeps the queue in sync and never posts.
No proxy or dedicated IP to buy for each account. The internet your team already has is the one Blowhorn uses.
No proxy pool to rent, assign, rotate or keep healthy, and no proxy setting to get wrong. Install, sign in, post.
No proxy or data center address for a site to flag. A teammate's own connection is the one the platform already knows for them.

solutions.prompt: Schedule the launch post for 9:00 Pacific, have every teammate's profile amplify it at 9:05, then --dry-run the rest.
solutions.major: Every soldier fires from their own foxhole. No rented trenches.

faq.q: Do I need a proxy?
faq.a: No. Blowhorn has no proxy setting. Each computer posts over its own internet connection, with its own IP address.

faq.q: Does anything post from Blowhorn's servers?
faq.a: No. Your account keeps the queue, schedule and run history in sync. Every action runs on one of your computers.

faq.q: Can teammates in different cities share one queue?
faq.a: Yes. Every computer signed in to your account works from the same queue, wherever it is, coordinated so the same post isn't sent from two computers.

faq.q: Do profiles on one computer get separate addresses?
faq.a: No. Profiles on one computer share that computer's connection. Separate addresses come from separate people on their own computers.

faq.q: Can I invite my team?
faq.a: Team invites are Coming soon. Today teammates install Blowhorn on their own computers, sign in to your account and add their own profiles.

faq.q: What if a teammate uses a VPN?
faq.a: Sites can see a VPN as well as a proxy. Check what a site sees in that teammate's browser.

link.label: Run the free check at Blowhorn Tells

solutions.name: Social scheduling
solutions.title: Blowhorn for social scheduling
solutions.headline: A scheduler that posts as you.
solutions.lead: Queue it once, like any scheduler. The difference is who presses Post: their servers, or your computers.
solutions.description: Schedule posts like any cloud scheduler, but your own computers press Post, as you, and Hacker News, GitHub and Slack join the same queue.

art.alt: Drill Instructor, a stocky turkey in a campaign hat with a whistle, holding the weekly schedule on a clipboard

pains.b: Cloud schedulers post through the vendor's app. You hand over access and they press Post.
Hacker News, GitHub and Slack still happen in tabs, outside the calendar.
Most schedulers publish one post. The profiles that would amplify it are left to remember.

gets.b: Every action runs on one of your computers, in your browser or through the platform's API. Your account keeps them in sync and never posts.
Hacker News, GitHub and Slack join LinkedIn, X, Reddit and Bluesky in one queue.
Schedule a post, then have every profile you run amplify it at the moment you pick.
Close your laptop. Another computer set up for that profile picks it up, as long as one of them is awake.

solutions.prompt: Move next week's posts into Blowhorn, add the Hacker News submission and the Slack note, then --dry-run.
solutions.major: Oh-nine-hundred means oh-nine-hundred. Your computers, your post.

faq.q: Does a computer have to be awake?
faq.a: One set up for the profile does. As long as one of your computers is awake, it covers the schedule. Each checks the queue about every 10 minutes.

faq.q: Where does the schedule live?
faq.a: In your Blowhorn account, so every computer you sign in on works from the same queue. Your account coordinates; it never posts.

faq.q: What about Instagram, TikTok, Facebook and YouTube?
faq.a: Coming soon.

solutions.name: LinkedIn automation
solutions.title: Blowhorn for LinkedIn automation
solutions.headline: LinkedIn automation without handing over your login.
solutions.lead: Blowhorn works LinkedIn in your own browser, signed in as you, at a human pace. No server logs in as you.
solutions.description: LinkedIn posting and careful outreach from your own browser, signed in as you: no password, 2FA secret or session cookie handed to a vendor's server.

art.alt: Trench Trooper, a muddy pig in a helmet holding a rifle with a teal tab bayonet and a gold periscope

pains.b: Growth tools ask for your password, your 2FA secret or your session cookie, then sign in as you from their cloud.
Some outreach tools sell going past LinkedIn's limits. Your account carries the risk.
You want careful LinkedIn hygiene, not a high-volume outbound funnel.

gets.b: Blowhorn does the typing and clicking in your own browser profile. No vendor server logs in as you.
Types key by key, pauses between actions and caps itself. CAPTCHA and 2FA always come to you.
Invite to your page, connect, accept invitations and withdraw stale ones. Flagged invitations are never auto-accepted.
Publish, reply and amplify on LinkedIn from the same queue as X, Reddit, Hacker News and the rest.

solutions.prompt: Withdraw LinkedIn invitations older than a month, accept the safe ones, then --dry-run invite for our page.
solutions.major: Hold the line, soldier. Your login stays in your browser.

faq.q: Is it ban-proof?
faq.a: No tool is. Blowhorn moves like a careful person, caps itself and stops for any challenge. Nobody can promise LinkedIn won't flag an account.

faq.q: Is it an outbound sequencer?
faq.a: No, and it doesn't pretend to be. It covers careful outreach: invite to your page, connect, accept and withdraw.

faq.q: Who signs in to LinkedIn?
faq.a: You do, in your own browser. Blowhorn types and clicks there, and LinkedIn's session cookies stay in the browser on each computer.

solutions.name: Multi-profile
solutions.title: Blowhorn for many profiles
solutions.headline: Many profiles. A real browser. No disguises.
solutions.lead: Every brand, founder and project you speak for, from one menu bar. Each profile runs in its own real browser profile, signed in as itself.
solutions.description: Run many brand, founder and project profiles from one desk: each in its own real browser profile, no fake fingerprints, from one coordinated queue.

art.alt: Mouse Marine, a mallard in a green beret riding a gold trackball on a small tank through teal water, cursor spear raised

pains.b: Antidetect browsers fake a fingerprint per profile. That's a disguise, and a hard one to explain.
Profiles live on one computer. Close it, or move to another, and the plan stays behind.
You still post by hand in every profile. There's no queue, no schedule and no amplify.

gets.b: Each Blowhorn profile maps to its own browser profile on each computer. No fake fingerprints.
One profile, one automation per platform, at a time. A second run waits rather than fighting the first.
Every computer you set up works from the same queue, coordinated so the same post isn't sent from two of them.
Schedule posts, amplify from every profile and dry-run first. Pause one action, one computer or all of them.

solutions.prompt: Queue this announcement for every brand profile on Thursday 10:00, have the founder profiles amplify it, then --dry-run.
solutions.major: One soldier, many uniforms. Every one of them real.

faq.q: Is this an antidetect browser?
faq.a: No. Blowhorn is a real browser, signed in as each profile. It does the typing and clicking.

link.label: See what sites can read about your browser

faq.q: Can two automations use one profile at once?
faq.a: Not on the same platform. While one run holds a profile's LinkedIn session, a second one waits. Different platforms can run side by side.

faq.q: Windows or Linux?
faq.a: Not today. Blowhorn runs on macOS 13 or newer, as the desktop app or the Python CLI.
